verdict: SHIP, scoped -- Q019/Q015 sense, caveats matter more than the label. Premise confirmed from source, not the write-up: IMyriadGenerator.Generate:GeneratorContext->Output (Types.fs:39-42, Output=Ast|Source) has no diagnostic channel and Program.fs either returns Some(Generate ctx) or prints OTHER:%A as free text (:167/:268) -- Myriad plugins genuinely cannot warn. All three rounds reproduced cell-for-cell (tooling worked): R1 Warning(5,12)-(5,17)/Error(6,12)-(6,22) both carrying 'This construct is deprecated. Q020 test message', ranges matching independently-located s.Bad/s.BadError; R2 backtick member 0 diagnostics + MYR099 present in GetDeclarationListInfo; R3 live FS0044(5,4)-(5,10) + EmitterA (5,39,5,43). EmitterA range checked independently (Meta at 0-based cols 38-42 -> rendered 39-43) -- note it anchors the type-annotation Meta (col 39), not the field name meta (col 33); 'field's declaration' in the design prose is loose. KILL out (falsifier passed: verbatim message with only FCS's fixed prefix, correct use-site range, severity flips both ways). REVISE's registered range trigger ('anchors the whole containing expression') specifically did NOT occur -- I drove eight extra consumer shapes and the anchor is always the member-access node (receiver+.member), NEVER the container: pipe/lambda/nested/argpos/if-then-else all leave the surrounding expression un-squiggled (longexpr anchors only s.Bad, not the conditional). So the mechanism generalizes better than the executor's 'just coarser' hedge for common code; two honest narrowings the write-up misses -- (a) worst case breadth is unbounded in the RECEIVER, not the container ((mkS 1234 5678 9012).Bad squiggles all 24 chars), (b) use-site means every TEXTUAL member reference: let getBad(x:S)=x.Bad fires at the helper definition, and the getBad s call site gets nothing, so a one-line helper hides the warning from all downstream callers. NULL does not fire cleanly because Visual Studio is a real host that runs TPs live and hosts no F# analyzer, so the TP channel is the sole live option there. But the caveats dominate: (1) the ONLY load-bearing new result is R1's obsolete-attribute use-site channel (real, reproduced, new to Thread 2 -- prior Q008/Q009/Q011 only threw at the static-argument site); (2) R3's 'cannot disagree' is TAUTOLOGICAL -- live.Message is FCS's prefix prepended to the exact same d.Message string DiagTP fed AddObsoleteAttribute, so the sameMessage substring check reads one shared immutable value twice and cannot fail on substance; it is two callers of a pure function agreeing, a plumbing result not a capability, the same trap Q019 R3 hit; (3) the two halves are UN-ENTANGLED -- EmitterA opens only SharedAnalysis, SharedAnalysis has no TP dependency, so a Myriad user wanting build-time diagnostics needs ZERO of the TP machinery, and that build-time half (the hypothesis's own 'more useful even if the TP fails' outcome) is not actually built: IMyriadGenerator is untouched and EmitterA is a 25-line standalone printfn format demo, not an API; (4) for Ionide an FSharp.Analyzers.SDK analyzer calling the identical SharedAnalysis.analyze STRICTLY DOMINATES (true declaration-site anchoring, arbitrary range, no obsolete hack, no synthetic members, fires without any preview provider), so the TP channel's unique niche is narrow twice over -- Visual Studio specifically AND only for a developer who has adopted the Q019-style erased Fields<file,record> preview provider and references its provided members (a VS user editing their own [<Lenses>] record gets nothing). R2's synthetic backtick member is legal and genuinely discoverable as claimed but of dubious value (a selectable int-returning fake member that pollutes completion, strictly worse UX than an obsolete attribute). Erased-vs-generative left untested (a real lift; FS0044 is not documented as erasure-specific but Q012's generative-resolution weirdness makes it genuinely uncertain, not obvious). Clean unqualified win: a provider can turn a self-detected structural limitation into a live, non-fatal, severity-tagged, use-site-anchored diagnostic with a verbatim custom message -- first in either thread, reproduced, generalizing past the one tested shape. Top follow-ups: build the real IMyriadGenerator diagnostics API (needs none of the TP half); build one analyzer and compare in Ionide; test a generative member; real-IDE host test.
